[F4 F5 F6] [RD-2 FARE-1]
C3: The driver cannot shelter behind RD-5: his own request came at 10:01 but the off-route segment did not start until 10:04, so at most the rider agreed in advance to 'go round via Halus Link' — and the 1.94 km detour that actually occurred (swinging up to 947 m off the optimal route) must be measured against that consent, not assumed from it; the burden is on the driver to show the agreed Halus Link routing equals the executed one. [F3 F7 F8 F9] [RD-5]

[F10 F11 F12] [RD-4]

[F15] [RD-6]

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.87)
events.body:
The trip contains exactly one off-route segment, the 10:04–10:07 diversion recording 1.94 km driven where the optimal line covers 0.22 km, i.e. 1.73 km extra peaking 947 m from the optimal route [F3]; the trip total was 11.7 km versus 9.9 km optimal (+1.8 km, +18%) [F1]. Under RD-1 each such segment is reviewed against RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5, and only a segment unexempted by any of them becomes a compensable detour [F1][F3][RD-1].

RD-5 is met here. The driver asked at 10:01 — before the segment's 10:04 start — "ok if I go round via Halus Link?" [F7], and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." at 10:01 [F8], which is exactly the "before you go" mutual agreement RD-5 requires; the driver's statement [F9] is consistent with the chat record [F7][F8][RD-5]. On scope, the rule is that a driver who names a road, area or route before leaving the optimal route and obtains agreement exempts that segment, unless the executed track plainly goes somewhere other than what was named. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment (10:04–10:07) in which 1.94 km was driven where the optimal route covers 0.22 km, adding 1.73 km of extra distance; the trip total was 11.7 km against a 9.9 km optimal route (+18%).

Because this RydeX fare is a fixed quoted fare that does not vary with trip distance — billed distance is 9.9 km, exactly the optimal distance, with no surge (1.0×) and no waiting fee — the extra 1.73 km did not itself increase the fare, so the refundable amount under the non-metered branch is limited to unpublished add-ons (here $0).

The driver cannot shelter behind RD-5: his own request came at 10:01 but the off-route segment did not start until 10:04, so at most the rider agreed in advance to 'go round via Halus Link' — and the 1.94 km detour that actually occurred (swinging up to 947 m off the optimal route) must be measured against that consent, not assumed from it; the burden is on the driver to show the agreed Halus Link routing equals the executed one.

The driver's 'traffic was building up' excuse fails RD-4: there is no traffic incident at all near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Tampines Expressway and Punggol Road — not band 1 or 2 (severe congestion) — and band evidence alone does not exempt a segment.

The rider paid $23.32 in total (base $3.90 + distance $14.02 + time $3.93 + platform $1.47), so if any portion of the fare is found attributable to the unexplained 1.73 km detour, that portion is quantifiable from the billed breakdown and should be refunded.

The driver's account carries 1 dispute upheld in the last 90 days (321 trips), so if the tribunal records an RD-1 breach here his conduct becomes repeated and warrants account review under RD-6; this flag rests on the profile record only and is requested as an add-on, not as the basis of the finding.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against us is F4: the billed distance (9.9 km) equals the optimal route exactly and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote, so under RD-2 the non-metered branch refunds only unpublished add-ons — F6 shows waiting $0.00, surge 1.0× and a $1.47 platform fee that is a published item, so the computable refund is $0 and the driver will argue RD-2 yields no_action.

F7 and F8 show the rider was asked at 10:01 'ok if I go round via Halus Link?' and answered 'Sure, go ahead.' before the 10:04 segment began; the driver will argue this is exactly RD-5 consent and kills the claim for that segment (F9 repeats it). Our counter — that 1.94 km driven vs 0.22 km optimal (F3) is far more than a Halus Link reroute — is inference from the GPS record, not a chat fact.
The rider's own profile (F14) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld, which the driver may use to paint a pattern of unsuccessful fare complaints.

F10/F11 show band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Tampines Expressway, so the driver will say there really was slowing traffic; our answer is that band 4 is not band 1/2 and F12 shows no incident, so RD-4(a)/(b) are not met.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment on this trip is the 10:04–10:07 diversion adding 1.73 km, and the driver proposed that diversion ('ok if I go round via Halus Link?') at 10:01, before the segment started, with the rider replying 'Sure, go ahead.' at 10:01 — so the rider agreed in advance to this exact route change.
Because the rider's pre-departure agreement covers the Halus Link diversion, that segment is not an unexempted detour and no route-deviation refund is due for it.
The trip is a RydeX fixed-quote job: the billed distance is 9.9 km, which does not exceed the 9.9 km optimal route, and surge is 1.0x, so the actual 11.7 km driven did not increase the fare at all.

The $23.32 total consists only of published components — base $3.90, distance $14.02, time $3.93, platform $1.47 — with waiting $0.00 and no post-trip manual add-ons, so there is nothing to refund under FARE-1.

Although the speed bands were only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and no incident was recorded (so RD-4(a)/(b) alone would not exempt the segment), the exemption here rests on the rider's prior agreement under RD-5, not on traffic evidence.
The driver's 90-day record shows only 1 dispute with 1 upheld and zero route disputes upheld, so RD-6's threshold for a repeated-route-offence account flag is not met.

weaknesses: The GPS record itself (F3) shows a real 1.73 km off-route segment peaking 947 m from the optimal route, and the trip was 1.8 km / 18% longer (F1) and 2.7 min slower (F2) than estimated — the rider will argue this looks like a detour regardless of consent.

The rider will press RD-4: there was no traffic incident near the route (F12) and only band 4 speed on both Tampines Expressway and Punggol Road (F10, F11), so the driver's stated reason (F9) is uncorroborated by any accepted traffic evidence.
The rider may argue the diversion went further than what 'go round via Halus Link' reasonably covered; the chat (F7, F8) contains no kilometre or route detail, and the agreement wording is general.

points.response: Conceded as to timing: the driver's request at 10:01 (F7) precedes the 10:04 start of the segment (F3), and the rider answered 'Sure, go ahead.' at 10:01 (F8), so RD-5's 'before' test is met for a Halus Link reroute.

RD-5 exempts only the route change the rider actually agreed to — 'go round via Halus Link' (F7) — and the executed segment drove 1.94 km where the optimal line covers 0.22 km, swinging up to 947 m off route (F3), so the driver must show that this specific track equals a Halus Link reroute; a consent to a named road cannot be stretched to cover an unnamed 1.94 km loop on the driver's say-so.
Accepted that billed distance equals the optimal 9.9 km with 1.0× surge, so under RD-2's non-metered branch the detour did not change the fare (F4, F5).
Accepted: the $23.32 breaks down into only published items with waiting $0.00 and no post-trip add-ons (F6), so no FARE-1 refund arises and I do not seek one.

The driver's own statement gives 'traffic was building up' as the reason for the diversion (F9), yet the only records are band 4 on Tampines Expressway and Punggol Road with no incident at all (F10, F11, F12) — so RD-4 supplies no exemption and the driver's sole support is an RD-5 consent whose scope (a named road, F7) does not match the 1.94 km executed loop (F3).

RD-6 is triggered only if this case itself results in an RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach; since the driver's own 90-day profile shows 1 upheld dispute (route: 0) (F15), a finding of breach here would make the conduct repeated within the 90-day window and, as an add-on to that finding, warrant account review (F14, F15).

Withdrawn as a claim under RD-5's concession of the Halus Link agreement: I accept the non-metered branch yields $0 refundable (F4, F5, F6), and I press only the RD-1 breach finding and the consequential flag.

The 1.73 km off-route segment is accepted as recorded, but its existence alone does not decide the case: RD-1 sends every segment through RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review, and this segment is answered by the rider's own prior agreement (F3, F7, F8).

We agree with the rider's own arithmetic and it is fatal to their claim: billed distance 9.9 km equals the optimal route and there are no unpublished add-ons (waiting $0.00, surge 1.0x), so the RD-2 non-metered branch yields a refundable amount of zero and no_action.

The rider's own message 'Sure, go ahead' at 10:01 (F8) precedes the segment start of 10:04 (F3), which is precisely the RD-5 test of agreement before leaving the optimal route; the driver did not, as RD-3(b) requires for unprotected self-chosen stops, pick a location silently — he named Halus Link in advance (F7, F9).

We do not rely on RD-4 at all: the exemption for this segment rests on RD-5 consent, so the absence of an incident (F12) and band 4 speeds (F10, F11) do not defeat the driver's case, and F10/F11 at least show the route was not free-flowing.

No portion of the $23.32 is attributable to the detour: the distance component is billed on 9.9 km, not the 11.7 km driven (F4, F6), so there is no computable overcharge to return under RD-2 or FARE-1.

RD-6 requires a finding against the driver AND route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 and the one upheld dispute is a no-show matter, so no flag_account can arise here (F15).

notices.text:
We looked into your dispute and are closing it with no refund.

The trip had one stretch off the best route, but the driver messaged you before it started asking whether he could go round via Halus Link, and you agreed. That agreement makes the stretch exempt, so it doesn't count as a compensable detour. Nothing else on the trip was off route.

Your RydeX fare was a fixed quote of $23.32, made up only of published charges, and the billed distance matched the best route. There's nothing to refund.

Your account is not affected, and no flag was placed on the driver.

We reviewed the dispute on this trip and are closing it with no action against you.

The single off-route stretch was the one you asked about beforehand — you named Halus Link and the rider agreed before you left the best route. That makes the stretch exempt, so no detour refund is owed. The fare was a fixed RydeX quote covering only published charges, so nothing is refundable.

No breach was recorded, so no account flag or review follows from this case. No further action is needed from you.
